prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1456; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Received first notice of loss from the claimant by phone. Insured reports a sideswipe while changing lanes on a multi-lane road. Claimant's vehicle was in the adjacent lane and sustained damage to the rear quarter panel. Claimant reports neck pain and stiffness and says they are being evaluated by their own doctor. No attorney involved at this time.

Entry 2: Obtained recorded statement from the insured. Insured states they checked the mirror and signaled but did not see the other vehicle until contact. Insured's vehicle has scrape damage to the right front bumper. Police report was not filed since no one requested one at the scene. Scene photos requested from insured.

Entry 3: Claimant emailed photos of vehicle damage and a copy of an urgent care visit summary listing whiplash and recommending follow-up in two weeks. Claimant asked whether the company will cover medical bills while the claim is open. Explained the general process for medical payment review and requested itemized bills when available.

Entry 4: Scheduled an independent appraisal of both vehicles. Appraiser noted the claimant's vehicle damage is consistent with a low-speed sideswipe and that the insured's bumper damage aligns with the claimant's rear quarter panel. Liability appears probable on the insured's side based on the lane change and the statement provided. Still awaiting the follow-up medical records.

Entry 5: Claimant called to check status and said they have not yet hired a lawyer and would prefer to resolve the claim directly. Reviewed the timeline for the repair estimate and provided a rental car option under the claimant's coverage. Claimant agreed to follow up once the physician's report is received. File remains open pending medical documentation and final liability review.
